commits.messageBody:
Replace the 91 existing int3 bodies with the compiler breakpoint intrinsic. This is the existing DllExport import-library template, whose runtime imports are redirected to the executable; no new feature stub is introduced.

The real isolated project builds under v120 Debug/Release on Win32/x64. Both Win32 configurations retain exactly the same 79 decorated exports. The separately pending owner-width API was included in that native candidate but does not alter the Win32 signature. Renderer linking and runtime delay-load resolution remain separate checks.
commits.messageHeadline: renderer: compile export-template breakpoints on x64

commits.messageBody:
Carry native owner addresses through allocation, tracking storage, reallocation, hooks and the exported allocator signature. Retain the legacy Win32 owner typedef for decorated ABI compatibility. Capture _ReturnAddress directly in each noinline x64 allocation wrapper; keep Win32 assembly.

Widen client stack storage to uint64 and mirror server-fork 74287848 native Windows walking and full DbgHelp serialization. The native x64 function-table pointer cache failed known-chain probes; bypassing only that cache restores them. Update all coupled address consumers and formats together.

Native v120 Debug/Release on Win32/x64: actual DebugHelp 257/257 captures each; instrumented real allocator DO_TRACK=1 and =5 each 2568/2568; five real allocation caller addresses match exact post-call instructions in every configuration (20/20). Direct3d9 hook imports match actual allocator definitions and template exports; Win32 export names unchanged.

Remaining limits: allocation-size narrowing, tracked reallocate(NULL) crashes, per-secondary-frame owner attribution, concurrent teardown/module unloading, final renderer export redirection and full client gameplay. No allocator or vendor substitute was used. Headless runtime is not covered.
commits.messageHeadline: memory: preserve allocator owner and call-stack addresses on x64
